question.value: Presence, physical properties, and dynamics of molecular clouds in Leo T

evidence.quote: Here we present the first detection candidates of CO in Leo T.
Using new CO data taken with the Atacama Compact Array to trace the H$_2$ content, we investigated the main features and properties of the molecular clouds identified in this work.
This paper uses the ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2024.1.00951.S.

configurations.value: 7m ACA configuration; single pointing; FoV ∼2.2×2.2 arcmin²

evidence.quote: The galaxy was observed with a single pointing using the 7m ACA configuration, with a field of view (FoV) of $\sim$2.2$\times$2.2 arcmin$^2$.

referee_caveats_inferred: Cloud dispersions are comparable to the 0.62 km s−1 channel width, with uncertainties comparable to or exceeding their values; virial masses and rotation need spectral-resolution checks.
Adjacent spaxels need not be independent within the synthesized beam; a quantified false-positive rate over the searched cube is absent.
Table 1 specifies size fits in MOM1 maps, while the main text describes fitting emission; the fitting image and beam-deconvolution treatment need clarification.
Table 1 calls surface densities upper limits, while the scaling-relation discussion calls them lower limits.
West-cloud velocity is 53.03 km s−1 in the spectral-fit text and 53.0 km s−1 in Table 1.
The luminosity equation prints pc−2, whereas Table 1 reports luminosities in pc².
Historic-SFR surface density is summarized as ∼10−3 in the main discussion and ∼6×10−3 M⊙ yr−1 kpc−2 in the detailed section.
North-cloud ejection depends on halo structure, an assumed 60 pc location, and a speed using only the line-of-sight component.
Several orbital-model references and parameter attributions are missing in the supplied text.
High upper limits on αCO do not by themselves establish equally high lower bounds on αCO.
